claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization and coercivity no greater than approximately 100 Oe.
The proposed starting material is single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a compositionally similar high-entropy alloy without secondary phases.
Controlled thermal annealing can initiate nanoscale coherent precipitation in an fcc FeCoNi-based matrix without complete phase separation.
Controlled ion irradiation can initiate nanoscale coherent precipitation in an fcc FeCoNi-based matrix without complete phase separation.
The treatment will create a multiphase nanocomposite containing nanoscale coherent precipitates embedded in an fcc matrix.
A treatment window exists that nucleates precipitates without completely decomposing the fcc matrix.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates act as pinning sites for magnetic domain walls.
Precipitate-induced structural inhomogeneities hinder domain-wall motion.
Hindering domain-wall motion through precipitate pinning increases coercivity relative to a single-phase alloy lacking such pinning centers.
Ion irradiation produces numerous coherent nanoscale precipitates in multiphase Al0.75CoCrFeNi and Al1.5CoCrFeNi alloys.
Ion irradiation did not produce precipitates in single-phase Al0.1CoCrFeNi even at a fluence of 1 × 10^16 cm^-2, corresponding to approximately 43 dpa.
The emergence of nanoscale precipitates under irradiation in multiphase AlxCoCrFeNi alters magnetic behavior.
The treatment will raise coercivity above approximately 100 Oe relative to untreated single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative.
The coercivity increase can be achieved while maintaining high saturation magnetization.
Precipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction will influence the coercivity response.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes irradiation-induced precipitation from a single-phase starting alloy, whereas the cited study reports no precipitates in its single-phase Al0.1CoCrFeNi alloy even at the highest irradiation fluence; precipitates appeared only in alloys that were already multiphase.
